zeta function. This method, the Riemann-Siegel formula, is the method of choice for

Following the terminology used by Edwards, call a Gram point gn good if it satisfies
Gram’s Law, and bad otherwise. Define a Gram block to be an interval [gn , gn+k ) such
that gn and gn+k are good Gram points but all Gram points strictly inside the interval
are bad. The process of counting roots on the critical line is then to simply count
the Gram points where Gram’s Law is satisfied, and to count the number of zeros of
Z(t) in each Gram block.
